title: Hierarchically Porous COFs Enabled by Copolymer‐Mediated Mechanochemical Preassembly
abstract: ABSTRACT The relatively small pore channels of conventional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) would impede mass transport and limit the accessibility of active sites therein, restricting their practical utility with bulky molecules. Here, we break this bottleneck by developing a copolymer‐mediated mechanochemistry strategy that enables the construction of hierarchically porous COF (HPCOF) precursors with tunable large mesopores, which are then recrystallized to afford crystalline HPCOFs. The confined microenvironments of low‐solvent ball‐milling not only enhance hydrogen‐bonding interactions between monomers and Pluronic F127 (PEO 106 PPO 70 PEO 106 ) micelles, but also eliminate the disruptive effects of excess solvent and acidic conditions on micelle assembly. Additionally, the mechanical pulses decompose the polycondensation into stepwise events, effectively buffering the incompatible rates between the polymerization of COF precursors and micelle assembly and allowing the mesostructures to be precisely “locked” under solid‐state confined conditions. By varying monomer combinations, seven representative HPCOFs with different connectivities were constructed. Thanks to its simplicity and reproducibility, the proposed strategy demonstrates potential in large‐scale production. Benefiting from the synergistic combination of large channels and rigid microporous crystalline walls, the resultant HPCOFs feature unique structural stability and favorable enzyme affinity, enabling efficient trypsin immobilization with retained catalytic activity for protein hydrolysis, prefiguring their application prospects in bioreactor construction.

title: Cofactor‐Inspired Second‐Sphere Engineering of Artificial Metalloenzymes for Neutral Ammonia Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Constructing artificial metalloenzymes with precisely positioned metal centers and tailored second‐sphere microenvironments remains challenging in replicating the hierarchical catalytic functions of natural enzymes. Here, we report a cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering strategy to construct an artificial nanozyme, CuS 1 /CN, featuring atomically defined [3Cu−1S] motifs selectively anchored to ultrasmall Cu clusters (∼0.73 nm) within a mesoporous nitrogen‐doped carbon framework. This architecture establishes enzyme‐like catalytic compartmentalization without compromising active‐site accessibility: exposed Cu sites mimic nitrate reductase for nitrate activation and water dissociation, while adjacent [3Cu−1S] motifs function as cofactor‐like centers that orchestrate interfacial hydration, facilitating proton‐coupled electron transfer and hydrogen relay during downstream hydrogenation. The engineered second‐sphere microenvironment overcomes the intrinsic *NO 2 ‐to‐*NO 2 H bottleneck and shifts the rate‐determining step to *NH 2 O‐to‐*NH 2 OH conversion with a substantially reduced energy barrier. Consequently, CuS 1 /CN enables highly efficient and selective ammonia electrosynthesis under neutral conditions at industrially relevant current densities with long‐term stability. Its integration into a Zn−NO 3 − battery further enables simultaneous nitrate conversion and electricity generation. This work establishes cofactor‐inspired second‐sphere engineering as a general strategy for designing artificial enzymes with programmable catalytic microenvironments beyond conventional active‐site engineering.

title: An Interfacial Electron Pump Enhanced Photo‐Assisted CO 2 ‐to‐Bioplastic Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Most solar‐ and electrochemical CO 2 ‐utilization strategies still terminate in small‐molecule products, whereas direct access to recoverable carbon products such as bioplastics remains uncommon. Here, we develop a photo‐assisted bioelectrochemical platform by coupling a Shewanella oneidensis MR‐1 bioanode functionalized with Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene quantum dots (MQDs) to a Cupriavidus necator biocathode modified with Ni‐doped carbon dots/poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (Ni‐CDs/PDDA). Cell‐associated MQDs form a conductive and photoactive biointerface, operationally described as an interfacial electron pump, that facilitates lactate‐dependent extracellular electron transfer (EET) under applied anodic bias and adds an illumination‐dependent current contribution. The MQDs‐enabled microbial fuel cell (MFC) delivers a peak power density of 0.82 ± 0.03 mW cm −2 under illumination. In the coupled CO 2 ‐fed system, anodic illumination raises polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB) productivity to 131 mg L −1 d −1 at −0.6 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (vs. RHE), approximately 47% above the matched dark value over a 12 h interval. The coupled platform reaches an apparent total‐energy‐to‐PHB efficiency of 3.42% when electrical, incident optical, and lactate‐derived chemical inputs are included. Multiscale analyses support an EET‐coupled interfacial relay involving cytochrome/heme‐associated components within the native EET network. This interface‐to‐synthesis strategy links photo‐assisted microbial electron harvesting to H 2 ‐mediated CO 2 ‐to‐PHB biosynthesis.

title: Enantioselective Access to Bis‐U‐Shaped Hexapyrrolic Expanded Porphyrinoids via a BINAM‐Directed Axial‐to‐Helical Chirality Transfer Strategy
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral expanded porphyrinoids hold great promise for chiroptical applications, while stereospecific access to enantiopure expanded porphyrinoids remains a significant challenge due to their conformational heterogeneity, tedious post‐synthetic resolution, and poor configurational stability. Herein, we employ 1,1'‐binaphthyl‐2,2'‐diamine (BINAM) as both the core building block and chiral directing group for the one‐pot stereospecific synthesis of a ‘ bis‐U‐shaped ’ hexapyrrolic expanded porphyrinoid platform. The axially chiral twisted conformation of BINAM imposes a strong conformational constraint during cyclization with tripyrrin subunits, inducing synchronous helical twisting of the conjugated chains and establishing multiple stereogenic helical elements. Single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction confirms quantitative transfer of BINAM axial chirality to persistent macrocyclic P / M helicity, affording enantiomers with exceptional thermal stability (no racemization even at 180°C). Notably, both Zn(II) and Co(II) bind via an unprecedented cross‐bridging mode, chelating dipyrrin donors from two separate tripyrrin units rather than undergoing conventional central insertion. This coordination rigidifies the folded framework, amplifies the chiroptical response (|g abs | values from 0.0096 to 0.0126 and 0.0137 for Zn(II) and Co(II) complexes, respectively), and directs homochiral supramolecular self‐assembly into one‐dimensional helical nanostructures in the solid state.

title: Guest-Mediated On-Surface Growth of 2D COF Heterobilayer for Synaptic Devices
abstract: Abstract Chemically defined organic heterobilayers offer a route to programmable interfacial coupling, yet their on-surface construction remains challenging due to the instability of dynamic covalent frameworks during sequential growth. Here, we report a guest-induced COF-on-COF growth strategy that enables deterministic heteroepitaxy of imine/boroxine covalent organic framework (COF) heterobilayers at solid–liquid interfaces. Coronene guest molecules occupy the pores of the underlying imine COF, stabilizing the framework while promoting interfacial molecular diffusion, thereby redirecting growth from framework degradation to directional epitaxy. This yields a structurally precise heterobilayer with a commensurate √3 × √3 R30° rotational relationship and long-range order. The resulting 2D COF heterobilayer is continuous over large areas with low defect density, enabling direct device integration without transfer. Electrical measurements, supported by theory, reveal interfacial charge redistribution arising from chemically encoded asymmetry, manifested as interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge trapping. Device responses, including nonvolatile switching and analogue conductance modulation, provide a macroscopic readout of the molecularly defined heterointerface. These results establish a route to programmable organic heterostructures in which interfacial growth, coupling, and electronic functionality are codesigned through molecular assembly.

title: Through‐Space Hot‐Electron Transfer Between Gold Nanoclusters and MOF Boosting Photothermal Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT The structural elucidation of metal nanocluster@MOF composites remains challenging due to their poor crystallinity, hindering the establishment of precise structure–property relationships. Here, we present a reverse templating strategy in which atomically precise gold nanoclusters (GNCs) to direct MOF crystallization, yielding highly crystalline GNC@MOF single crystals for single‐crystal x‐ray diffraction (SCXRD) analysis. Coarse‐grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) simulations reveal the adaptive growth of MOFs around spherical GNC template, accompanied by a complete topological transformation from rectangular to hexagonal symmetry. Combining transient absorption spectroscopy, density functional theory (DFT) calculations, and optoelectronic measurements, we reveals pronounced space interfacial electron coupling between GNCs and MOFs. This coupling facilitates directional transfer of photoexcited hot electrons from GNCs to MOFs, resulting in enhanced photothermal conversion performance. Upon 660 nm laser irradiation, Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF rapidly heats to 106.3°C within 6 s and reaches a maximum temperature of 182.0°C (∆ T = 158.1°C), outperforming discrete Au 13 clusters (∆ T = 126.3°C) under identical conditions. Au 13 @Zn‐NDC‐MOF also exhibits excellent photostability over multiple on‐off cycles. This work establishes a direct link among through‐space interfacial electron coupling, hot‐electron transfer, and enhanced photothermal behavior, providing a generalizable platform for the rational design of high‐performance MNC@MOF materials for solar energy conversion and photocatalysis.

title: Topology-Based Generation of Hypothetical Metal−Organic Frameworks through Single-Metal Nodes and Symmetry-Aware Linker Rotation
abstract: Abstract Topology-based hypothetical metal−organic framework (MOF) generators enable scalable exploration of chemical space beyond experimentally reported structures, but their accessible design space is constrained by the building blocks and assembly rules they encode. Here, we present PORMAKE2, an upgraded topology-based hypothetical MOF generator designed to improve both access to small-pore structures and geometric fidelity. PORMAKE2 introduces an expanded building-block library, including single-metal nodes, and implements symmetry-aware linker rotation for higher-fidelity framework assembly. These upgrades substantially expand the accessible small-pore MOF space and enable MOF designs that were inaccessible to earlier workflows, including ZIF-type and CALF-20-like structures with improved geometrical agreement. Carbon dioxide direct air capture (DAC) and xenon/krypton separation are included as case studies demonstrating that an improved framework-generation workflow can influence downstream screening outcomes. These results establish PORMAKE2 as a more expressive and chemically faithful front-end platform for hypothetical MOF generation.

title: Diatom‐Inspired Hierarchical Macro‐Mesoporous AuPd/ZnO with Topology‑Induced Metal‐Support Interactions for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Bacterial Volatile Biomarkers
abstract: ABSTRACT Inspired by the hierarchical porous architecture of diatom frustules, we report a biomimetic hierarchically ordered macroporous mesoporous AuPd/ZnO composite as a high‐performance sensing platform for trace detection of 3 ‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (3H2B), a critical volatile biomarker of Listeria monocytogenes. Here, the deliberate design of high curvature mesopores as topological traps to anchor AuPd nanocrystals, proposing a topology‐induced metal‐support interaction mechanism that triggers interfacial electronic restructuring. This confinement‐driven modulation optimizes oxygen reactivity and reduces the reaction energy barrier, enabling MEMS sensor with an ultralow detection limit of 9.7 ppb and high response (R a /R g = 74.4) to 10 ppm 3H2B at 150°C, significantly outperforming conventional porous materials. In situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations reveal that Pd sites within the AuPd alloy serve as primary electron donors, facilitating 3H2B dehydrogenation and oxidation. Furthermore, a portable wireless module integrated with a random forest algorithm allows accurate identification of 3H2B in complex mixtures, validating real‐time monitoring of bacterial growth in food. This work not only establishes a paradigm for precision synthesis of hierarchically porous materials but also provides profound insights into interfacial science by leveraging topological confinement to tailor electronic structures for interfacial catalytic performance and food safety applications.

title: Directional Nitrite Spillover Couples to Interfacial Hydrogen-Bond Networks for Ampere-Level Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction to ammonia is often constrained by the proton-coupled hydrogenation of adsorbed nitrite (*NO2), a step commonly accelerated through hydrogen spillover and local reactive-hydrogen (*H) supply. This hydrogen-centered view, however, treats *NO2 largely as a passive intermediate and overlooks whether its migration can reconstruct the interfacial hydrogen-bond-network environment required for downstream hydrogenation. Here, we show that directional *NO2 spillover couples site-specific intermediate transport with interfacial hydrogen-bond-network reorganization. In a Cu–Ag dual-site model interface, nitrate activation and *NO2 formation occur preferentially on the Cu sites, whereas migrated *NO2 species are stabilized and hydrogenated on the Ag-associated sites. In situ spectroscopy, kinetic isotope measurements, distribution-of-relaxation-time analysis, and theoretical simulations reveal that this Cu-to-Ag relay enriches K+-associated interfacial water, reinforces hydrogen-bond connectivity, and facilitates *H delivery for *NO2 hydrogenation. The optimized CuAg N-doped carbon (CuAg–N-C) achieves near-unity Faradaic efficiency (FE) for NH3 with a yield rate of 411.8 mmol g–1 h–1 and retains 83% FE at 1 A cm–2 in a flow cell. The catalyst further retains substantial nitrate-to-ammonia recovery in simulated and authentic industrial water matrices. More broadly, this work establishes *NO2 spillover as a dynamic interfacial mechanism linking intermediate transport, water-network organization, and proton-coupled nitrogen conversion, providing a framework for sustaining molecular-scale selectivity under chemically complex reaction environments.

title: Zeolite Crystallization via Seed-Mediated Chemical Vapor Deposition
abstract: Abstract The demand for zeolites with specific, tailored characteristics is expected to further accelerate. For decades, however, zeolites have been predominantly synthesized by hydrothermal methods, in which tightly coupled sol–gel processes, nucleation, and crystal growth constrain property control and complicate device-oriented fabrication. Here we report the direct synthesis of zeolites by chemical vapor deposition (CVD), in which vapor-delivered precursors crystallize on preexisting zeolite seeds. Mechanistic investigations reveal that zeolite growth under CVD follows a fundamentally distinct pathway, where vapor-phase hydrolysis–condensation reactions are spatially decoupled from interfacial crystallization. This decoupling enables the maintenance of a controlled and steady supersaturation, offering a facile strategy for fabricating zeolite films with low dielectric constants and robust mechanical properties. The unique mechanism and operation mode of CVD bring zeolite crystallization into a manufacturing-relevant vapor-phase regime that could be extended to other zeolite types and deployed in diverse applications.

title: Advances in Conductive Self‐Adhesive Interfaces for Epidermal Bioelectronics: Materials Design, Fabrication Strategies, and Future Directions
abstract: ABSTRACT Epidermal bioelectronics require a reliable, low‐impedance skin–electrode interface that maintains conformal contact under dynamic conditions. Conductive self‐adhesive interfaces, which integrate charge transport with interfacial adhesion, offer a compelling solution. However, optimizing conductivity, adhesion, mechanical compliance, and biocompatibility simultaneously remains challenging due to inherent trade‐offs among these properties. In this review, we first discuss the physicochemical properties of skin, then systematically examine the adhesion mechanisms, charge conduction pathways, and biocompatibility evaluation protocols for conductive self‐adhesive interfaces. We then comprehensively review recent advances in three primary material design strategies—structural engineering, surface‐confined assembly, and bulk blending molding—comparing their respective advantages and disadvantages in balancing the four core properties. Furthermore, we discuss the application of pre‐fabrication‐integration and in situ fabrication techniques in constructing stable and reliable interfaces. Building on these material platforms, we highlight their implementation in representative epidermal bioelectronics, including electrophysiological monitoring, physicochemical sensing, therapeutic intervention, and human–machine interfacing, with particular emphasis on how interface properties dictate device performance in each scenario. Finally, we identify remaining challenges and propose future directions for the continued development of conductive self‑adhesive interfaces toward practical epidermal bioelectronic applications.

title: Sunflower pollen microgels enable sonication-free dispersion of carbon nanotubes for bio-based conductive inks
abstract: Sustainable, high-performance conductive inks are crucial for wearable electronics. While biopolymer-based dispersants offer renewable and biocompatible routes for CNT inks, a paradox persists: biopolymers require energy-intensive extraction, high-power ultrasonication, and lack the rheological strength for precision extrusion printing. Here we show that a sonication-free strategy utilizing sunflower pollen microgels in their native granular state, leveraging their amphiphilic spiky architecture, achieves CNT debundling through a mild-stirring-driven capture-collision-friction integrated process, while alginate provides electrostatic stabilization. The resulting pollen-alginate-CNT (PAC) inks exhibit rapid thixotropy and high viscoelasticity, enabling high-fidelity 3D extrusion and screen printing. Drying induces a lamella-like assembly, forming anisotropic conductive networks. These features unlock multifunctional performance, including humidity sensing via interlayer-spacing modulation, direction-dependent strain sensing, and electromagnetic interference shielding. This work establishes a scalable, energy-efficient framework that overcomes the processing and rheological limitations of conventional bio-based inks, advancing sustainable, adaptive printed electronic systems. Dispersing carbon nanotubes in conductive inks often requires energy-intensive sonication. Here, the authors use sunflower pollen microgels and alginate to create sonication-free conductive inks for printing, sensing, and electromagnetic shielding applications.

title: When Electrolytes Become Dopants: Programming Charge Transport in Conductive Metal−Organic Framework Transistors
abstract: Abstract Conjugated metal−organic frameworks (c-MOFs) operating in ionic environments have emerged as promising microporous and conductive systems for next-generation applications. Understanding the interplay between electrolyte composition and electronic−ionic mixed transport remains a critical barrier to the rational design of novel devices. Here, we demonstrate that electrolyte composition provides a direct and programmable handle for controlling charge transport and field-effect properties in c-MOF electrochemical transistors (ECTs). Two types of c-MOF thin films composed of the conjugated linker 2,3,5,6,10,11-hexahydroxytriphenylene (HHTP) and either Cu2+ or Ni2+ ions, namely, Cu3(HHTP)2 and Ni3(HHTP)2, were employed as transistor channel materials. Using these c-MOFs as prototypical conductive frameworks, we systematically interrogate the influence of ionic strength, ion identity, pH, and gate configuration on transistor operation. Across these variables, we unveil robust and quantitative relationships linking the nature and conditions of the electrolyte to variations in charge neutrality, modulation of transconductance, and transitions between transport regimes. For instance, increasing ionic strength shifts the transfer curves of Cu3(HHTP)2- and Ni3(HHTP)2-based ECTs toward a more negative potential, with a linear dependence on the logarithm of ion concentration. The ion-hydrated radius strongly influences ion-electron transport, as smaller cations more readily permeate the framework and reduce surface potential. Charge neutrality point potential (VCNP) displays a linear pH dependence, with sensitivities comparable to conducting polymer ECTs. Device performance is also influenced by the gate electrode configuration (liquid-junction or pseudo-reference electrodes). Extensive field-effect characterization demonstrates good electrochemical stability. A unified mechanistic model successfully describes the coupled ionic−electronic transport governing c-MOF device operation.

title: Synergistic Molecular-Nano Engineering Enabling Ultralong-Cycling and High-Capacity Lithium Storage of Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: Abstract Lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) combine the high energy density of batteries with the high-power density of supercapacitors for potential advanced applications. As promising anode candidates for LICs, the practical application of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is hampered by the intrinsically low electronic conductivity. Here, a “molecular-nano” dual-scale synergistic strategy is proposed to enhance the charge transport and utilization of active sites. At the molecular scale, three highly crystalized COFs (2,6-DAAQ-COF, 2,6-DAA-COF, and 1,4-DAAQ-COF) via donor-acceptor (D–A) structural design are synthesized to enhance the intramolecular charge separation and electron transfer processes. At the nanoscale, a three-dimensional conductive network is constructed by in situ compositing with carbon nanotubes (CNTs) to yield core-shell structured COF@CNT, which also effectively exfoliates COF layers and exposes active sites. Benefiting from the synergistic enhancement between intramolecular charge transfer and the macroscopic conductive network, the optimized 2,6-DAAQ-COF@CNT50 exhibits exceptional lithium storage performance, retaining a high discharge capacity of 1983 mAh g–1 after 1000 cycles at 1 A g–1. Furthermore, the electrode also exhibits excellent electrochemical performance at low temperature (–20 °C), retaining 220 mAh g–1 after 2000 cycles at 0.5 A g–1. The assembled LICs demonstrate superior stability of up to 10,000 cycles. This study provides a new strategy and mechanistic insights for designing high-performance organic anode materials for LICs.

title: Reticular Programming of Gold Nanocluster Electronic States Enables Near-Unity Faradaic Efficiency in Nitrate-to-Ammonia Electrosynthesis
abstract: Achieving selective nitrate-to-ammonia electrosynthesis requires more than accelerating nitrate activation: the catalyst must sustain eight-electron reduction while preventing premature intermediate release and competing hydrogen evolution. Yet controlling these competing processes through the molecular architecture surrounding well-defined metal centers remains challenging. Here, we report the first application of gold nanocluster covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to electrocatalytic nitrate-to-ammonia conversion, establishing reticular connectivity as a strategy for programming catalytic electronic environments. Four crystalline frameworks (KIN-1–KIN-4) were constructed from a common pyrazolate-bridged Au3 cluster and structurally differentiated organic linkers. Despite preserving predominantly Au(I) centers, the frameworks exhibit distinct frontier electronic-state distributions, pore architectures, and electrochemical selectivities. The triformylphloroglucinol-linked KIN-2 delivers a near-unity ammonia Faradaic efficiency of 99.5% at −0.70 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode, with an ammonia productivity of 0.75 mg h-1 cm-2 and only 0.8% Faradaic efficiency toward nitrite. Isotopic labeling verifies nitrate-derived ammonia formation, while in situ attenuated total reflectance surfaceenhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry reveal evolving reactionassociated signatures. Density functional theory identifies preferential *NO hydrogenation through *NHO rather than NOH, with respective uphill free-energy increments of 0.66 and 1.36 eV, alongside unfavorable hydrogen adsorption (ΔGH* = +1.62 eV). These findings demonstrate that reticular construction can differentiate reaction energetics without changing the metal’s formal oxidation state, offering a molecular design principle for directing multielectron electrocatalysis toward desired products.

title: Planar-Chiral Metal Clusters Direct Polarization-Responsive Supercrystals
abstract: Abstract Chiral metal clusters are promising atomically precise building blocks for hierarchical chiral materials, but their programmed assembly into structurally resolved supercrystals with traceable chirality transfer remains challenging. Here, we show that planar-chiral Cu5 clusters can serve as symmetry-defined modules for constructing polarization-responsive supercrystals. Through single-site capping control and symmetry-matched linker-directed coordination assembly, the Cu5 unit is organized into monomeric, dimeric, trimeric, and helical crystalline architectures, thereby enabling chirality to be traced from discrete clusters to higher-order supercrystalline structures. Single-crystal analyses reveal how the planar chirality of the cluster is encoded locally and propagated through distinct, orientationally ordered packing sequences. Quantitative Mueller matrix measurements show architecture-dependent circular and linear optical responses, including circular and linear retardance, which correlate with the crystallographic orientation and packing sequence of the Cu5 units, particularly Cu···Cu bonding. This work establishes planar-chiral metal clusters as versatile, stereochemically programmable synthons, providing a quantitative framework that links cluster-level chirality, arrangement orientation, and macroscopic polarization-dependent optical responses. The strategy offers a novel modular route to structurally defined chiral supercrystals, in which optical polarization responses can be traced to atomically resolved anisotropic sequences of chiral cluster assembly.

title: Colloidally Prepared Homogeneous Wide-Bandgap Perovskites for Efficient Tandem Solar Cells with Industrial Silicon
abstract: Abstract Wide-bandgap (WBG) perovskites, based on mixed halide-cation compositions, are widely employed as top cells in perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells to overcome the theoretical limitations of single-junction devices and exploit the full potential of crystalline silicon photovoltaics. However, uncontrolled nucleation rates and disordered crystallization kinetics in WBG perovskites pose a grave challenge to the preparation of phase-homogeneous perovskite films. Herein, we identify the undesirable precursor suspension as the main underlying reason for the compositional inhomogeneity and propose a colloidal engineering strategy to reconstruct the perovskite intermediate complex. According to classical colloidal theory and theoretical calculations, long-chain alkylphosphonic acid molecules are selected to precisely regulate colloidal structures and properties via their specific coordination strengths, leading to colloid-guided rapid nucleation and slow crystallization processes. Assisted by the uniform colloidal nucleation template, the prepared WBG perovskite films with compositional homogenization and reduced trap density enable tandem devices based on industrial silicon heterojunction cells to yield a champion power conversion efficiency of 34.01% (a certified reverse-scan PCE of 33.65%) for a 1 cm2 active area. The resultant encapsulated tandem device maintains 93% and 88% of its initial efficiency after 1211 h and 1000 h of one-sun operation at 25 and 65 °C, respectively, under their maximum power points.

title: Non‐Precious Metal High‐Entropy Oxide Sub‐1 nm Nanowires for Li‐O 2 Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Highly active and structurally robust cathode catalysts are critically required to boost the electrochemical performance of lithium‐oxygen batteries (LOBs). Herein, a generally synthetic method of non‐precious metal high‐entropy oxide‐polyoxometalate sub‐1 nm nanowires (NPMHEO‐POM SNWs) has been successfully developed induced by POM clusters under mild solvothermal conditions. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations reveal that the dominantly driving forces for the assembly of POMs and multi‐metal oxides are the Coulomb and van der Waals forces, enabling precise theoretical guidance for targeted material synthesis. Benefiting from the 1D ultrafine structure with fully exposed active sites, the precise adjustment of components optimizing the adsorption capability of intermediate (LiO 2 *) and discharge product (Li 2 O 2 ), and the strong interactions of multi‐metal oxides and POMs contributing to the stability, the BiVZrNiCeO x ‐phosphomolybdic acid SNWs‐based LOB achieves a highly specific capacity of 9944 mAh g −1 and stable cycling durability for 312 cycles at 500 mA g −1 , highlighting their great promise as high‐efficiency electrocatalysts for advanced LOBs.

title: Electronic Polarization of Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for Precise Antibiotic Purification
abstract: Abstract Precise molecular separation is essential for pharmaceutical production and purification, yet existing sieving systems struggle to distinguish structurally similar molecules due to their predominant reliance on size exclusion. Herein, we fabricate a covalent organic framework (COF) membrane featuring fluorine-induced polarized nanochannels for fast organic solvent nanofiltration. The incorporation of fluorine atoms redistributes electron density along the pore walls, creating a polarized electrostatic environment while lowering surface energy. This unique pore environment promotes the uptake and transport of polar solvents, while enhancing separation selectivity by retarding highly polar solutes through polarity-dependent solute-framework interactions. Furthermore, the low surface energy imparted by the robust C–F bonds also reduces irreversible foulant adhesion and facilitates permeance recovery after cleaning. The resultant COF membrane achieves a molecular weight cutoff down to 350 Da and stable operation for over 550 h. Notably, it differentiates structurally related fluoroquinolone antibiotics according to their molecular polarity and delivers a favorable separation factor of 8.9 for norfloxacin over its synthetic intermediate piperazine. This work demonstrates that engineering pore-wall polarity in COF membranes provides a viable route to chemically regulated molecular recognition beyond size-based separation.

title: Engineering Amino‐Induced p‐π Conjugation for Electronic Regulation of Li + Transport in PVDF‐Based Solid‐State Electrolytes
abstract: ABSTRACT Sluggish Li + transport in poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF)‐based solid polymer electrolytes (SPEs) arises from restricted polymer segmental motion and persistent Li + ‐FSI − association, while conventional fillers provide limited regulation of the local electronic and coordination environments. Herein, amino‐functionalized UiO66‐NH 2 is introduced into a PVDF/lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide (LiFSI) electrolyte to construct electronically active composite SPEs (U6NP). The electron‐donating ─NH 2 groups induce p‐π conjugation, redistribute the linker electron density, and strengthen ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT)‐related electronic coupling between the organic linkers and Zr‐O clusters. This electronic reconstruction, together with amino‐associated modulation of local O‐centered coordination environments, reshapes the electrostatic landscape, weakens Li + ‐FSI − interactions, and facilitates Li + migration. U6NP delivers a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.41 × 10 −3 S cm −1 , a Li + transference number of 0.56, and an oxidative stability of 4.42 V. More importantly, Li||U6NP||LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) cells with a cathode loading of 21.5 mg cm −2 retain 98.51% after 120 cycles at 0.05 C. The Li||U6NP||NCM811 pouch cell delivers 136.6 mAh g −1 initially and 120.9 mAh g −1 after 100 cycles. This work establishes ─NH 2 ‐induced p‐π conjugation‐enhanced LMCT as an effective strategy for electronically active MOF‐reinforced PVDF electrolytes toward high‐loading solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Self‐Confinement‑Tailored Energy Routing for Superior Thermal‐Adaptive Ln‐MOFs Scintillator
abstract: ABSTRACT Noncontact radiation monitoring in extreme environments is essential across scientific and industrial fields, driving the development of x‑ray scintillators. Conventional scintillators continue to suffer from inadequate exciton utilization, poor thermal stability, or limited processability. In this study, we propose a self‐confinement strategy to tailor energy routing for constructing superior thermal‐adaptive scintillators. Two lanthanide‐organic frameworks, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln and Ln‐BDC‐F, are rationally designed and synthesized. Compared with the free state of pure ligand or its quasi‐confinement state in Ln‐BDC‐F, ZJNU‐1006‐Ln exhibits a strong molecular self‐confinement state arising from compact ligand packing, thereby enhancing exciton utilization, suppressing nonradiative energy dissipation, and optimizing the energy routing. These features endow ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with superior radio‐luminescent performance, including high light yield (max ∼ 62,000 photons MeV ‒1 ), low detection limit (92.7 nGy air s ‒1 ), and great thermal‐stability (< 7% emission intensity attenuation from 77 to 590 K). ZJNU‐1006‐Ln membranes and fibers demonstrate great potential for in situ, real‐time x‐ray imaging and radiation monitoring. In addition, by tracking radio‐luminescent chromaticity, a series of ZJNU‐1006‐Ln with varied Tb 3+ /Eu 3+ doping ratios enables precise localization of radiation‐exposed regions over a broad temperature range, particularly encompassing the Earth surface temperature window. This work highlights the self‐confinement effect as a promising strategy for designing advanced inorganic‐organic scintillators.

title: Spatial Electrostatic Complementarity in MOF Pores Enables Selective Recognition of Closely Related Fluoromethanes
abstract: ABSTRACT Trace purification of chemically similar gases is particularly challenging when molecular size and kinetics offer little contrast and conventional affinity descriptors provide conflicting guidance. Trifluoromethane (CHF 3 ) removal from monofluoromethane (CH 3 F) exemplifies this problem: CH 3 F has the greater dipole moment, and CHF 3 is more polarizable. Here, to our knowledge, we report the first adsorptive removal of trace CHF 3 from CH 3 F and demonstrate electrostatic complementary recognition (ECR) in interpenetrated anion‐pillared MOF pores. Localized, directional negative‐potential sites from TiF 6 2– pillars and surrounding electropositive pyridyl C─H domains complement the 1H/3F electrostatic pattern of CHF 3 while geometrically frustrating the inverse 3H/1F pattern of CH 3 F. All other benchmark adsorbents showed an overall preference for CH 3 F, whereas both TIFSIX frameworks achieved a reversal of adsorption preference toward CHF 3 under trace‐relevant conditions. TIFSIX‐Cu‐dpt, featuring a more focused and directional ECR environment, adsorbed 18.5 cm 3 /g of CHF 3 at 0.1 kPa. Neutron diffraction, adsorption thermodynamics, and molecular simulations support a spatially complementary multipoint binding mode. Fixed‐bed breakthrough of a binary feed containing 1000 ppm CHF 3 produced CH 3 F with >99.999% purity relative to CHF 3 at 320 L/kg. These results show how spatial electrostatic complementarity can translate subtle molecular differences beyond conventional scalar descriptors into selective adsorption.

title: Localized Geometric Frustration in One‐Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks for Photocoupled Electrocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocoupled electrocatalytic two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) offers a promising route to H 2 O 2 production, yet integrating photoinduced charge separation with bias‐driven interfacial electron transfer to enhance H 2 O 2 selectivity remains challenging. Here, we examine localized geometric frustration in a 1D benzothiazole‐based covalent organic framework (TDBT‐COF) as one structural feature associated with the 2e − pathway, using isoreticular naphthalene‐based TDNT‐COF and thiazolo[5,4‐d]thiazole‐based TDTT‐COF for comparison. The benzothiazole‐based monomer exhibits a 6.86° connection‐angle disparity that narrows to 1.38° in TDBT‐COF, reflecting partial accommodation by the periodic lattice. Under illumination, TDBT‐COF achieves 92% H 2 O 2 selectivity, exceeding those of TDNT‐COF (58%) and TDTT‐COF (66%) and its dark‐state selectivity (65%). During photocoupled electrocatalysis, TDBT‐COF delivers the H 2 O 2 production rate of 3.73 mol g −1 h −1 with a Faradaic efficiency of 91.9%. Theoretical calculations reveal greater electron transfer to adsorbed O 2 and lower *OOH formation barriers in TDBT‐COF than in the reference COFs. Photoexcitation further facilitates these interfacial processes. Locked‐relaxed fragment calculations give TDBT‐COF a larger strain energy and *OOH adsorption shift, in line with localized geometric frustration. This is the first study introducing the concept of localized geometric frustration to COF‐based photocoupled electrocatalysis, offering a structural perspective for catalyst design.

title: Setaria viridis-inspired hierarchical Co3O4/CoS nanowire/nanosheet architecture on carbon cloth for advanced lithium storage
abstract: Abstract To overcome the severe volume variation and intrinsically low electronic conductivity associated with Co 3 O 4 , a Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC composite was constructed via sequential hydrothermal synthesis and electroprecipitation. This material employs flexible carbon cloth as the substrate, on which arrays of cobalt tetroxide (Co 3 O 4 ) nanowires are first grown, followed by the electrodeposition of cobalt sulphide (CoS) onto the nanowire arrays. When evaluated lithium-ion batteries, the Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC electrode delivered an initial discharge specific capacity of 1152.38 mA h g − 1 at 0.1 A g − 1 . After 200 charge-discharge cycles, it retained a reversible capacity of 613.07 mA h g − 1 with a coulombic efficiency of 99.72%. Under a high loading current of 500 mA g − 1 , the average discharge capacity reached 578.92 mA h g − 1 . The biomimetic Setaria viridis -inspired hierarchical architecture endows the Co 3 O 4 /CoS@CC electrode with excellent long-term cycling durability and outstanding rate performance, which provides an enlarged specific surface area, an efficient conductive network, and improved structural robustness, thereby significantly enhancing the electrochemical performance.

title: Self-Assembly of Sub-10 nm Lamellar Domains with Controlled Orientation Using Fluorinated Junctions
abstract: Abstract We studied the thin-film self-assembly behavior of low-molecular-weight symmetric block copolymers (BCPs) of poly(solketal methacrylate) (PSM) and polystyrene (PS), with and without a poly(hexafluoroisopropyl acrylate) low-surface-energy (LSE) junction, PSM-b-F-b-PS and PSM-b-PS, respectively. An in situ hydrolysis of the PSM block to hydrophilic poly(glyceryl monomethacrylate) (PGM) markedly increased the segmental interaction parameter, χ. The high-χ, low-N copolymers self-assembled into horizontal or vertical lamellae with a center-to-center distance between adjacent lamellae (full pitch) of 9.4 nm. A free-energy analysis of the thin-film self-assembly on native Si predicted that the LSE junctions would induce an orientation of the lamellae for PGM-b-F-b-PS normal to the surface with only a few segments of the LSE junction. In comparison, an orientation of the lamellae parallel to the surface with an island-hole surface topography resulted from PGM-b-PS. We note that vertical lamellae were observed at the edges of islands and holes where the thickness transits from one thickness commensurate with the full pitch to another. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and grazing-incidence small-angle X-ray scattering (GI-SAXS) results matched the free-energy predictions. With LSE junctions, uniform vertical orientation of the self-assembled lamellae was obtained, eliminating the need to modify the substrate or apply external fields to obtain this orientation, significantly simplifying preparation.

title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-contaminated wastewater into value-added ammonium products offers a promising pathway, yet practical implementation is hindered by sluggish nitrate reduction kinetics and poor redox rate matching in paired electrolysis systems. Here we report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that enables kinetically synchronized nitrate reduction and sulfate oxidation for the direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate ((NH4)2S2O8). In situ spectroscopic measurements and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations show that the PdP2@Cu3P heterointerface catalyst dynamically shuttles active hydrogen from hydrogen-generation sites to nitrate-activation sites, revealing rapid P-mediated hydrogenation at the interface, thereby decoupling hydrogen production from consumption and bypassing the multistep proton-coupled electron transfer pathway. The catalyst achieves a nitrate reduction rate of 8.94 × 10⁻7 mol cm⁻2 s⁻1, an ammonia Faradaic efficiency exceeding 92%, and sustained operation at 220 mA cm⁻2. In a membrane-electrode paired electrolyzer, the system produces (NH4)2S2O8 at a rate of 1.6 mmol h⁻1 cm⁻2, with 55% lower energy consumption and ~99.6% lower CO2 emissions than conventional routes. This work establishes a general strategy for nitrate–sulfate wastewater valorization and high-value oxidant production. Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

title: Co‐Assembly and Metal‐Ion‐Driven LCST Engineering in Programmable Supramolecular Nanoarchitectonics for Climate‐Adaptive Energy‐Efficient Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving energy‐efficient control of solar radiation requires intelligent materials capable of dynamically responding to environmental stimuli. Thermoresponsive systems exhibiting lower critical solution temperature (LCST) transitions offer an attractive strategy for passive and reversible modulation of light transmission. Herein, we report three xanthone‐based bolaamphiphiles with varying oxyethylene chain lengths that undergo thermoresponsive supramolecular self‐assembly in water. The resulting spherical nanoaggregates exhibit temperature‐dependent light scattering, enabling reversible switching between transparent and opaque states. XFO 2 and XFO 3 display distinct LCST transitions at 10°C ± 0.03°C and 33.14°C ± 0.03°C, respectively. Stoichiometric mixing of XFO 2 and XFO 3 enables programmable LCST regulation across 10°C–33°C through mixed/co‐assembled supramolecular states with minimal thermal hysteresis. XFO 3 further exhibits metal‐ion‐driven LCST modulation in the presence of Fe 3 + and Al 3 + . Leveraging these complementary tuning strategies, a 24 × 24 cm 2 prototype demonstrates rapid reversible optical switching between 30°C and 37°C and stable operation over 6000 cycles across 12 months. High solar (ΔT so l = 88.6%) and infrared (ΔT IR = 87.5%) transmittance modulation further demonstrates the potential of this supramolecular platform for climate‐adaptive, energy‐efficient smart‐window technologies.

title: Antiaromaticity for Through-Space Molecular Thermoelectricity
abstract: Abstract Charge transport in molecular junctions has largely relied on aromatic frameworks, where intramolecular π-delocalization stabilizes the electronic structure but inherently limits intermolecular electronic coupling. Here we show that antiaromatic Ni(II) norcorrole assemblies outperform their aromatic counterparts in thermally driven charge transport. This superior performance arises from strong intermolecular coupling, facilitated by the externalized electronic stabilization of antiaromatic building blocks. Such strong intermolecular coupling enables unusually thick molecular stacks within molecular junctions and yields Seebeck coefficients of up to 600 μV K–1, far exceeding those of the aromatic analogue. Quantum transport calculations reveal that π–π stacking in the antiaromatic assemblies shifts the HOMO transmission resonance closer to the Fermi level while progressively narrowing it, accounting for the substantial enhancement of the Seebeck coefficient while maintaining efficient long-range charge transport with a low tunneling attenuation coefficient. These findings establish antiaromaticity as a design principle for thermoelectric energy conversion based on collective intermolecular coupling rather than isolated molecular orbitals.

title: Regulating Functionalized MXene Crystal-Field Splitting toward Efficient Bifunctional Oxygen Electrocatalysis of Lithium–Oxygen Batteries
abstract: Abstract MXenes offer fast conductive frameworks with abundant intrinsic active metal sites, making them promising cathode catalysts for lithium–oxygen batteries for addressing sluggish oxygen kinetics and severe cathode passivation. However, the predictive electronic descriptors for rationally regulating these intrinsic active sites remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of crystal-field splitting engineering at Ti sites of Ti3C2-MXene to achieve bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysis. Through coordinated anionic and cationic modifications, we regulate the local coordination environment of Ti atoms, weakening crystal-field splitting and promoting electron delocalization within Ti3C2-MXene frameworks. X-ray absorption spectra reveal systematic shifts of Ti K-edge and contraction of the pre-edge splitting, consistent with weakened and distorted Ti ligand fields. This electronic rearrangement promotes an asymmetric Li2O2 adsorption configuration, thereby lowering the energy barriers for both ORR and OER. Consequently, the functionalized Cu–Ti3C2Br2 delivers a high discharge specific capacity of 11,662 mAh g–1 and reduces the initial charge overpotential by 50% compared with Ti3C2OF. This study indicates crystal-field splitting as a key descriptor governing oxygen electrocatalytic behavior in lithium–oxygen batteries.

title: Multifunctional Conductive Nanoporous Carbon Honeycombs for Electrothermal Direct Air Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct air capture (DAC) requires sorbent contactors that can process large air volumes with minimal pressure drop while enabling rapid, energy‐efficient regeneration. A multiscale conductive honeycomb contactor based on nanoporous amorphous carbon (NAC) is presented, in which adsorption‐active porosity, mechanical support, electrical conduction, and Joule‐heat generation are integrated within the same continuous framework. The fully interconnected NAC pore network accommodates epoxide‐functionalized polyethyleneimine while preserving CO 2 ‐accessible transport pathways after binder‐assisted shaping into a mechanically robust monolith. Straight‐through honeycomb channels enable low‐resistance airflow with efficient CO 2 capture, whereas the conductive NAC walls act as volumetric heating elements positioned directly adjacent to the CO 2 ‐binding phase for fast regeneration. The optimized contactor achieves a volumetric adsorption productivity of up to 0.32 mmol cm −3 h −1 while maintaining a specific fan‐energy demand below 10 J m −3 . Direct Joule heating enables more than 95% desorption within 16 min under the laboratory N 2 ‐purge protocol, approximately twofold faster than external heating under the same conditions, with no measurable capacity loss over a 15‐cycle short‐term test. The key advance is the simultaneous integration of high volumetric capacity, accessible nanoporous transport, mechanical robustness, low‐resistance airflow, and electrothermal regeneration within a single honeycomb contactor.

title: Synchronized Charge Transport and Mass Transfer via a Laser‐Programmed Spatial Interface Strategy for Scalable H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Synchronizing ultrafast charge transport with slower molecular mass transfer remains a central challenge for scalable H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Here, we introduce a laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy that patterns carbon nitride supported on a porous titanium mesh into adjacent pristine regions and dual‐defect microregions bearing cyano and nitrogen‐vacancy defects. Multiphysics simulations and potentiometric scanning electrochemical microscopy measurements suggest that this spatial architecture produces a localized potential response near the catalyst‐liquid interface, while in situ fluorescence microscopy indicates enhanced local O 2 availability. This coupled response is proposed to bridge the intrinsic timescale gap by facilitating directional extraction of photogenerated electrons while accelerating interfacial O 2 enrichment. The defect microregions promote proton‐coupled sequential two‐step O 2 reduction, whereas the conductive titanium mesh suppresses local electron accumulation and carbon nitride self‐photocorrosion. The optimized L‐CN/TM‐PS2 produces 2538 µmol L −1 g −1 H 2 O 2 within 120 min and achieves approximately 98.6% Escherichia coli inactivation. This work establishes the laser‐programmed spatial interface strategy as a design principle for synchronizing charge transport and mass transfer in supported photocatalysts for continuous‐flow environmental disinfection.

title: Cyclic Dimer Acceptor towards 20.9% Efficient Organic Solar Cells by Suppressing Electron‐Phonon Coupling
abstract: ABSTRACT Minimizing non‐radiative recombination energy loss (Δ E nr ) remains a critical challenge in boosting the efficiency of organic solar cells (OSCs). Herein, we report a novel cyclic dimer acceptor, CR‐L8, rationally designed via an asymmetric linking strategy. In this molecular architecture, a thiophene linker extends the conjugated plane, while a flexible 1,6‐di(thiophen‐2‐yl)hexane chain acts as the another linker, synergistically modulating molecular conformation, packing, and aggregation. Compared to its linear analogues, the cyclic configuration significantly suppresses molecular vibrations and electron‐phonon coupling, leading to a substantially enhanced photoluminescence quantum yield and effective blockage of non‐radiative recombination channels. Importantly, CR‐L8‐based blend maintains favorable molecular packing and double‐fibril morphology, ensuring efficient charge transport. As a result, the D18:CR‐L8 device achieves a record efficiency of 17.23%, which is the highest value reported to date for OSCs employing cyclic dimer acceptor. Moreover, the Δ E nr of 0.155 eV in D18:CR‐L8 device is the lowest among OSCs with efficiencies exceeding 15%. Finally, incorporating CR‐L8 as the third component into D18:L8‐BO blend further boosts the performance, with the optimized ternary device achieving an impressive efficiency of 20.92%. This work pioneers a cyclic acceptor design strategy that mitigates non‐radiative recombination, offering a new molecular blueprint for high‐performance organic photovoltaics.

title: Structural Engineering of Bio-Alkaloid Ionic Liquid-Mesoporous Silica Nanohybrids for Optimized Transdermal Atopic Dermatitis Therapy
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) are highly promising drug carriers owing to their exceptionally large surface area and tailorable pore structures for high drug-loading capacity, but their transdermal delivery is severely restricted by the skin barrier. Integrating natural ionic liquids (ILs) can modulate skin permeability; however, the mechanistic impact of distinct IL molecular structures on the interfacial properties of MSN-IL nanohybrids remains poorly understood. In this study, we engineered a structure-specific transdermal delivery platform by assembling citric acid-functionalized MSNs with various natural bio-alkaloid cations (choline, L-carnitine, and matrine). Density functional theory (DFT) and macroscopic physicochemical evaluations revealed that the matrine-based system (CA-M 1:2) forms a highly stable, tight ion-pairing conformation. This specific configuration endows the formulated MSN-IL nanohybrid with a robust dynamic viscosity, providing effective steric occlusion to prevent premature drug leakage within the MSN pores. Despite this internal cohesion, in vitro assays and transmission electron microscopy confirmed that the CA-M 1:2 hybrid dynamically facilitated the highest transdermal flux, transporting intact MSNs across the skin barrier via an IL-associated enhancement of skin permeation. In the atopic dermatitis mouse model, topical treatment with the optimized DEX/MSN-IL system significantly accelerated lesion resolution, restored epidermal architecture, and suppressed inflammatory cascades by downregulating IFN-γ, TNF-α, and IgE levels. This work establishes a physical chemistry-driven molecular-to-macro framework for the rational design of structure-specific nanohybrids, advancing high-performance topical therapeutics for inflammatory skin diseases.

title: Emergent mesoscale nanoparticle patterns from a non-equilibrium liquid lens
abstract: Colloidal nanoparticles can assemble into richly structured materials, yet the complex morphologies that emerge under non-equilibrium conditions are often viewed as irreproducible artifacts. Here we show that evaporating a lens-shaped colloidal suspension at a fluid–fluid interface produces a robust cascade of nanoparticle film morphologies, ranging from continuous monolayers to perforated films, ribbon networks, and isolated tiles. Using in situ confocal microscopy and ex situ electron microscopy together with coupled cross-scale simulations, we identify the physical principles that govern this sequence. A macroscopic transport model determines the deposition history imposed by evaporation, which drives a nanoscale kinetic Monte Carlo model capturing particle rearrangement and solvent-mediated kinetic arrest. A coarse-grained Cahn–Hilliard–Stokes framework rationalizes the observed mesoscale periodicity as a finite-wavelength instability of the evolving film. By tuning concentration and solvent volatility, we control the system’s trajectory through this dynamic phase space and establish a predictable framework for navigating non-equilibrium nanoparticle assembly. Nanoparticle assembly at fluid interfaces is often viewed as unpredictable and dominated by uncontrolled non-equilibrium effects. Here, the authors show that evaporation-driven nanoparticle assembly reveals predictable morphologies through multiscale modeling, linking transport dynamics and kinetic arrest.

title: A Metal–Organic Framework-on-Metal–Organic Framework Chemical Nose for Intelligent Identification of Depression-Related Biomarkers via Machine Learning
abstract: Abstract Depression is a complex mental disorder associated with dysregulation of multiple neurotransmitter-related biomarkers, including Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, and 5-HTP. Herein, we report a MOF-on-MOF fluorescent sensor array, RhB@ZIF-8-on-FL@UiO-67, for simultaneous discrimination and detection of these biomarkers. Spatial separation of dyes within the hierarchical architecture effectively suppresses fluorescence crosstalk and generates multiple independent luminescent channels, enhancing signal diversity and sensing performance. The resulting multidimensional fluorescence responses enable accurate identification of Try, 5-HT, 5-HIAA, 5-HTP, and their mixtures. Both LDA and HCA achieved a classification accuracy of 100% for the tested samples. Furthermore, machine learning models, including BP, RF, DT, SVM, and KNN, confirmed the robustness of the sensing platform. This work integrates MOF-on-MOF engineering with machine learning-assisted pattern recognition, offering a sensitive and reliable strategy for multiplex biomarker analysis and providing a promising approach for intelligent diagnosis of complex diseases.

title: Covalent–Organic Frameworks for Food Waste Prevention: From Molecular Programming to Preservation, Sensing, and Packaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Food waste is a major global sustainability challenge, generating substantial economic losses and environmental burdens across production, distribution, and consumption. Covalent–organic frameworks (COFs), with their predictable composition and topology, tunable pore architectures, high crystallinity, and chemically addressable frameworks, provide a versatile platform for molecular‐level functional design. This review presents a function‐oriented perspective on COFs for food waste prevention. We first discuss how pore size, topology, surface chemistry, framework organization, and hierarchical transport pathways can be programmed to regulate molecular adsorption, confinement, release, and transport, thereby supporting preservation‐related functions. We then examine fluorescent COFs and COFs‐based nanozymes as complementary optical and catalytic signal‐transduction platforms for monitoring food quality deterioration and contamination markers, with emphasis on their construction strategies and underlying photophysical and catalytic mechanisms. These structure–function relationships are further discussed in the context of preservation and shelf‐life extension, food quality deterioration and contamination sensing and monitoring, and functional food packaging. Finally, key challenges associated with structural stability, mass transfer, functional integration, scalable synthesis, safety, and practical deployment are highlighted. By linking molecular programming with functional transduction and food‐system applications, this review provides design principles for advancing COFs toward more effective food waste prevention.

title: Mechanocatalytic Upcycling of Diverse Plastic Wastes via an Fe/SiO 2 Catalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling plastic waste into high‐value chemicals is an attractive pathway for the sustainable development of human society. Here, we demonstrate the mechanocatalytic conversion of polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, polyester, and their mixtures into valuable hydrogen (H 2 ) and methane (CH 4 ) gases on an iron (Fe) species‐dispersed silica (SiO 2 ) catalyst, achieving almost 100% conversion under mild conditions. During the mechanocatalytic process, Fe species from the milling balls were anchored to the surface of pristine SiO 2 nanoparticles, forming the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst. Simultaneously, the Fe and Si sites in the Fe/SiO 2 catalyst synergistically facilitate the C─H bond activation and C─C bond cleavage pathways, enabling a favorable dehydrogenation‒cracking‒hydrogenation process to produce commercially valuable H 2 and CH 4 . Notably, this catalytic system also exhibits exceptional versatility in processing mixed plastic wastes without requiring prior sorting, while maintaining robust cycling stability. No expensive components, toxic chemicals, or energy‐intensive thermal conditions are needed.

title: Toward clinical utilization of fullerenes: physicochemical characterization of the fullerene derivative C60-ser self-assembly into hollow monolayer associates in aqueous solutions
abstract: In aqueous solutions fullerene derivative C 60 -ser undergoes spontaneous, thermally reversible self‐assembly to form hollow, water-filled associates with hydrodynamic diameters ranging from tens of nm to 1 μm. Associate diameter increases with temperature (positive ∂d/∂T) and decreases with concentration due to nucleation-limited growth rather than a thermodynamic equilibration. Electron microscopy establishes that each associate is a close-packed monomolecular shell of C 60 -ser molecules (shell thickness δ ≈ 3 nm) enclosing a water-filled interior; with the shell contributing a minute fraction to the total volume at all conditions studied. Van’t Hoff analysis of the temperature-dependent size data yields positive values for ΔH° and ΔS° on the classical entropy-driven, hydrophobic-effect influenced self-assembly of associates mediated by cooperative intermolecular hydrogen bonding and solvent reorganization energy. Unlike aqueous, organic solutions result in nearly all C 60 -ser molecules being non-associated even at 4 °C, demonstrating that the cooperative hydrogen-bond network of water provides the dominant thermodynamic driving force for associate formation. Surface tension measurements (γ ≈ 0.071 N/m) confirm the absence of classical amphiphilic behavior. Zeta potential measurements (ζ = −9 at 4 °C and monotonously rising to −6 mV at 44 °C) are concentration-independent in the 0.1−10 mg/mL range, consistent with a small intrinsic negative surface charge, and suggestive of colloidal stability being governed by hydration repulsion from surface hydroxyls more than from electrostatic double-layer forces, operating independently of the entropy-driven bulk association equilibrium. The associates are kinetically labile: they are disrupted by passage through a 20 nm syringe filter and reform within seconds, consistent with low per-molecule net stabilization energy. The same lability rules gravitational behavior: under centrifugal force stratification remains far below what a static, non-exchanging population of this size would produce, showing that resistance to gravitational phase separation is itself a consequence of rapid monomer exchange. This is the first report of thermodynamic quantification (ΔH° &gt; 0, ΔS° &gt; 0) and XDLVO modeling for a hollow, water-filled fullerene nanocapsule, which occupies a unique structural and thermodynamic niche distinct from other reported small-molecule self-assembling systems of non-amphiphilic, hydrogen-bond-driven, thermodynamically reversible hollow associate formation.

title: Cationic Gemini Surfactants with Cleavable Spacer and Tails as Multifunctional Bioactive Platforms: Self-Assembly, DNA Binding, Gene Transfection, and Antibacterial Activity Studies
abstract: Abstract Cleavable surfactants have gained significant interest in surfactant science due to their controlled degradation, improved biocompatibility, and potential applications in biomedical and industrial fields. The development of cleavable Gemini surfactants, which offer superior surface activity and self-assembly behavior compared with conventional single-chain surfactants, provides a promising approach toward multifunctional and biodegradable surfactant systems. Herein, we report the design and synthesis of two novel cationic Gemini surfactants, C14E-EE-EC14 and C14E-AA-EC14, featuring strategically engineered cleavable spacer architectures containing diester and diamide functionalities, respectively. In addition to the cleavable bonds incorporated within the spacer, both surfactants contain ester linkages connecting the hydrophobic tails, resulting in four hydrolytically cleavable functionalities within the molecular framework, which enhance biodegradability and reduce potential toxicity. Their physicochemical properties were systematically investigated using surface tension, conductivity, isothermal titration calorimetry, and fluorescence probe studies. Both surfactants exhibited excellent surface activity and spontaneous self-assembly, while the chemical nature of the spacer linkage strongly influenced their aggregation thermodynamics and microenvironmental properties. Transmission electron microscopic analysis revealed distinct morphology governed by spacer rigidity, where the diester-linked surfactant formed smaller micellar aggregates along with vesicular structures, whereas the corresponding diamide-linked derivative generated elongated aggregates and smaller vesicular assemblies. The cationic Geminis showed efficient DNA interaction, confirmed by ethidium bromide exclusion assays and molecular docking studies. This improved complexation ability resulted in effective gene delivery, with both surfactants demonstrating comparable transfection efficiency to TurboFect in RAW 264.7 cells. Additionally, their surface-active characteristics translated into remarkable antibacterial activity against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria, comparable to kanamycin and ampicillin. Overall, these cleavable Gemini surfactants represent promising multifunctional platforms combining biodegradability, tunable self-assembly, gene delivery capability, and antimicrobial activity.

title: Correlating the Solution Aggregation and Crystallite Orientation in n-Type Conjugated Polymers
abstract: Abstract The ability to control the crystallite orientation of conjugated polymers in the solid state is critical for enhancing their charge-transport properties. Compared with significant advances achieved for p-type conjugated polymers, control over the crystallite orientation of n-type conjugated polymers remains somewhat limited. Herein, two naphthalenediimide (NDI) polymers (NDI-2T and NDI-3T) were selected as model systems to investigate the formation and transformation of edge-on and face-on modes through solvent selection and post-processing thermal and solvent vapor annealing. In CHCl3, NDI-2T and NDI-3T exhibited weak and strong aggregation, resulting in respective face-on and edge-on modes in as-cast films. In chloronaphthalene (CN), their enhanced aggregation happened during the solution-to-film process, leading to more pronounced edge-on orientations. Furthermore, these two crystallite orientations of NDI-2T films were reversibly transformed through combined heating and solvent vapor annealing. These crystalline behaviors were closely related to their aggregation in solution, providing insights into the crystallization of n-type copolymers for optoelectronic applications.

title: Interfacial Electrochemical Reconstruction Enables Direct Regeneration of Graphite Anodes
abstract: Abstract Graphite anodes are structurally robust and remain largely intact after battery cycling, yet their recycling remains rarely implemented in lithium-ion batteries. Their electrochemical degradation is dominated not by bulk structural collapse but by the accumulation of resistive and heterogeneous solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers at the electrode–electrolyte interface. Here we report an interfacial-selective recycling strategy based on electrochemical SEI decomposition (ESD) that directly targets this interface-limited degradation mechanism. By applying a controlled linear potential ramp, ESD selectively oxidizes and removes unstable organic SEI components while reconstructing a thin and uniform inorganic-rich SEI. This process restores Li+ transport pathways and effectively reduces interfacial resistance without introducing bulk defects. Importantly, because ESD directly treats the recovered electrode without material separation, the existing electrode architecture, including the active material, binder, conductive additive, and current collector, can be preserved and reused. As a result, ESD-treated graphite exhibits near-complete recovery of reversible capacity and improved cycling stability in half cells, as well as pronounced performance recovery in full cells after long-term cycling. These findings establish interfacial electrochemical reconstruction as a low-energy and sustainable pathway for graphite anode recycling and reuse.

title: Multidimensional Kinetic Optical Spectrometry of Dynamic Liquid Systems: Applications to Molecular Assembly and Liquid−Liquid Phase Separation
abstract: Abstract Dynamic liquid systems are commonly characterized by sequential optical measurements that independently monitor extinction, scattering, fluorescence, or optical anisotropy. Because these complementary observables are acquired at different time points, reliable temporal correlation among evolving optical processes remains a fundamental analytical challenge. Here, we establish multidimensional kinetic optical spectrometry (MKOS) as a general analytical strategy for simultaneously characterizing dynamic liquid systems. Using a previously developed multitrack linearly polarized spectrometer, UV−vis extinction, polarization-resolved scattering, fluorescence, and depolarization are acquired concurrently from a single sample with sub-second temporal resolution, generating multidimensional optical fingerprints of evolving physicochemical states. The analytical capability of MKOS is demonstrated using meso-tetrakis(4-sulfonatophenyl)porphyrin (TSPP) molecular self-assembly and elastin-like polypeptide (ELP) liquid−liquid phase separation. Simultaneous measurements reveal kinetic relationships inaccessible to conventional sequential spectroscopy, including the decoupled evolution of extinction, scattering, and fluorescence during TSPP assembly, the dependence of assembly pathways and resulting optical fingerprints on sample preparation history, and irreversible structural reorganization induced by thermal annealing. Application to ELP further demonstrates that multidimensional optical fingerprints resolve reversible thermal phase separation, quantify transition kinetics, identify the maximum coacervation rate at 53.2 ± 0.5 °C and the maximum decoacervation rate at 48.9 ± 0.7 °C for heat−cool cycles from 20 to 60 °C, and distinguish structurally stable and unstable coacervated states under different isothermal conditions. Beyond these representative systems, this work establishes MKOS as a broadly applicable analytical framework for interrogating dynamic liquid systems through simultaneous correlation of complementary optical observables, providing substantially richer mechanistic and kinetic information than conventional sequential spectroscopic measurements.

title: Hydroxy-Functionalized n-Type OMIECs as Multifunctional Conductive Biointerfaces for Simplified Biosensor Fabrication
abstract: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) have emerged as key materials for bioelectronics owing to their ability to couple ionic and electronic transport. However, their potential as multifunctional biointerfaces for biosensing remains largely untapped, particularly for n-type systems. Here, we report a hydroxy-functionalized n-doped poly(benzodifurandione) (PBFDO-OH) that unifies efficient electron transport and enzyme immobilization within a single material platform. By introducing terminal hydroxy groups into the polymer backbone, PBFDO-OH enables the direct immobilization of glucose dehydrogenase through a simple one-pot strategy, eliminating the gold substrates, self-assembled monolayers, and multistep surface activation protocols that underpin conventional biosensor fabrication. This streamlined approach yields robust biofunctional electrodes with enhanced electrochemical performance while preserving enzyme activity and long-term stability. Integrated with additively manufactured electrodes, the resulting glucose biosensor demonstrates a high sensitivity of 17.4 μA L mmol-1, a low detection limit of 3.42 μmol L-1, excellent reproducibility (RSD = 5.35%), reliable quantification in human serum (RSD < 10%), and outstanding operational stability over three weeks (RSD < 3%). Beyond glucose sensing, this work establishes a general materials design strategy in which chemical functionalization transforms n-type OMIECs into conductive biointerfaces that simultaneously simplify device fabrication and provide stable bioreceptor integration for next-generation bioelectronic technologies.

title: Investigating comparative controlled drug release behavior of various types of inorganic ordered mesoporous silica nanomaterials as a carrier for anticancer drug vinorelbine tartrate
abstract: Vinorelbine tartrate, a semisynthetic anticancer drug freely water soluble, is selected for investigating various types of nanoparticles in controlling its release by encapsulating them. Vinorelbine tartrate available in oral and IV formulations has been found to be cytotoxic, causing neutropenia along with common side effects of gastrointestinal disturbances related to its drug delivery. Nanomaterials applications are completely dependent on its shape and size and well documented in the literature for its successful research outcome. These ordered mesoporous range silica nanomaterials (5–40 nm). The Present study was focused on investigating various types of ordered mesoporous silica nanomaterials like SBA-15, SBA-16, COK-12, and KIT-6 as a controlled release carrier of anticancer drug vinorelbine tartrate. The selected nanomaterials encapsulated with vinorelbine tartrate formulated into controlled release tablets by direct compression method. The post compression parameters of all the formulations were found to be in acceptable criteria. Characterized by FTIR, SEM and UV-visible spectrophotometric methods for compatibility and morphological study, DTA, TGA & in vitro drug release percentage in 6.8 pH phosphate buffer solution. Total of 13 formulations prepared (V1–V13) & compared, of them V2 found to be best controlled release nanomaterial carrier suitable as tablet dosage forms with 27.79% at the end of 150 min.
